title: Documents: Licence, Insurance, MOT & Tax
whatItIs: To drive legally you need a valid licence, insurance, vehicle tax and, for older cars, an MOT certificate.

keyFacts.text: You MUST have at least third-party insurance to drive on a public road.
A car MUST normally have its first MOT at 3 years old, then every year.
A vehicle MUST be taxed to be driven or kept on a public road. With a SORN, it MUST be kept off the road.

keyFacts: The V5C registration certificate shows the registered keeper, not necessarily the owner.
Tell DVLA when you change your name or address, or sell the car.

items.title: Driving licence
items.text: Must be valid for the vehicle you drive. Keep your address up to date.

items.title: Insurance
items.text: At least third-party cover to drive on a public road.

items.title: MOT
items.text: First at 3 years old, then every year. Shows the car met the minimum standard.

items.title: Vehicle tax
items.text: Needed to drive or keep the car on a public road.

items.title: V5C logbook
items.text: Shows the registered keeper. Tell DVLA about any changes.

items.title: SORN
items.text: Declare it if you keep an untaxed vehicle off the road.

a.label: Third party only
points: Covers damage to others, not your car

b.label: Comprehensive
points: Covers others and your own car

onTheTest.question: When does a car need its first MOT?
onTheTest.why: In Great Britain a car needs its first MOT when it is 3 years old, and then every year.

traps: The V5C shows the keeper, not who owns the car.
Third-party cover doesn't pay for damage to your own car.
An MOT doesn't mean the car stays roadworthy all year: keep checking it.

sources.ref: Annex 3 (Motor vehicle documentation and learner driver requirements)
